The human plateau began to shift. Posts spread across feeds like wildfire: it was prime time, right before the end of the workday. Two hundred thousand viewers instantly jumped to two hundred and fifty. Online media bots picked up the event and started churning out news about a provocative stream by “the most innovative business coach of our generation.” And a woman, no less!

Now three hundred and fifty thousand people from all around the globe were watching, liking, sharing, and paying real dollars to ask Freja a question. Three hundred and sixty. Three hundred and seventy. Every new thousand took Freja’s breath away. And then came the time to answer.

The main thing was not to let this interaction with her followers devolve into a group Tinder date.

*“Do you have kids?”* a stranger asked. *“How do you achieve success when you have four of them?”*

Freja wanted to reply, *“You don’t.”* But first of all, stay-at-home moms on maternity leave made up forty-eight percent of her audience, so it was a sore spot. And second, you couldn’t give an answer like that to a subscriber who had most likely scraped those fifty bucks together out of her kids’ lunch money. So Freja went with a polite, pre-rehearsed response.

“Everyone defines success for themselves,” she said. “If you’ve always dreamed of being a mom or a dad, then your children *are* your capital. The key is to stick to your investment strategy and not hand your capital over to unvetted funds.”

*“Are you married?”* someone asked, donating the five-dollar minimum.

Freja had already learned to leave questions like that unanswered. Fortunately, a flood of more interesting (and pricier!) questions flushed all the cheap provocations straight down the drain.

Besides, her joke had landed. The chat was ecstatic, and viewership was climbing: a clip of her answer had already gone viral on Twitter. Yet with fame comes responsibility—the questions took a sharp turn into group-Tinder-date territory.
